messages:
karim: heads-up: onboarding hit a weird one with the Go generator sample app. user closes tab, handler returns, but SDK still prints tokens and a goroutine hangs. minimal repro attached. feels like internal background tasks ignore req cancel.

karim: repro (very small):
```go
func Serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    it := client.Generator("mini").Stream(r.Context(), Prompt{Text: "idea"})
    for it.Next() {
        if _, err := w.Write([]byte(it.Text())); err != nil {
            log.Println("write failed", err)
            return
        }
    }
    if err := it.Err(); err != nil {
        log.Println("iter err", err)
    }
}
```

liv: seen this pattern a lot. root causes: (1) auth refresh/reconnect uses context.Background() so it ignores request cancel; (2) iterator internals block on transport read with no user-facing cancel.

sam: +1. i think we should do two things: expose an explicit Stop()/Shutdown API on the iterator for user-initiated teardown, and provide an opt-in config to propagate a parent ctx into internal background tasks so retries/auth don't outlive request.

karim: Stop() sounds good. suggested semantics: non-blocking Stop() that signals shutdown and returns immediately, plus StopWait(ctx) to wait for teardown with timeout. that keeps handler ergonomics simple. e.g. call Stop() on write error then return, or StopWait(ctxWithTimeout) when you need to wait for cleanup.

sam: concrete API sketch:
```go
type GenIter interface {
  Next() bool
  Text() string
  Err() error
  Stop()          // best-effort, non-blocking
  StopWait(ctx context.Context) error // blocks until shutdown or ctx done
}
```
Also add a client option: WithCancelPropagation(parentCtx context.Context) or builder style: client.Generator("x").WithParentCtx(r.Context()).Stream(...). That way SDK internals (auth refresher, reconnect) use the provided parent and will cancel when request does.

liv: love the builder option. backwards-compatible: keep default behavior but document the footgun of Background in sampleapps. new sampleapps should use WithParentCtx(r.Context()) when the iterator lifecycle is tied to the request.

karim: implementation notes: Stop() should close the internal event channel and cancel the transport ctx; StopWait should cancel then wait on an internal done channel. be careful with races: Next() may be blocked on a net.Read; ensure Stop cancels the underlying connection. tests: unit test where fake server continues sending after Stop and ensure Next returns within 50ms. integration: auth-refresh midstream + Stop should cancel reconnect attempts.

sam: also add a small README cookbook: HTTP handler pattern -> create iter with WithParentCtx(r.Context()) or call Stop() on write error. add explanation of when to prefer Stop vs parent ctx propagation.

docs-bot: action: update Go SDK README + sampleapps to demonstrate Stop/StopWait and WithParentCtx. add a line about avoiding Context.Background() in auth/refresh paths.

ci-bot: CI: go-sdk/streaming-tests queued — will run after PR.

liv: i'll draft the PR with the API shim and two sampleapp updates using Stop() on write errors, plus a test harness (net.Pipe fake server). will also grep repo for Context.Background() in auth/refresh paths and include a cleanup TODO.

karim: thanks — that should make onboarding less confusing. i'll paste the repro link into the PR. :rocket:
